annotationRationale: Finite geometric sums encode the repeated-digit integers. Comparing two lengths forces equations on the integer digits, whose bounded possibilities are then exhausted and checked for sufficiency.
sourceMethod: Follows the official method of reducing the equation to a linear relation in 10^n and subtracting the relations for two lengths. The substitution t=10^n shortens the algebra, and reversibility establishes that the valid triples work for all positive n.

review.mathCheck: For t = 10^n > 1, the equation reduces reversibly to (9c−a²)t = 9b−9c−a². Two distinct t values force a² = 9c and b = 2c. The only valid digit triples are (3,2,1) and (6,8,4), both valid for every positive n. The maximum sum is 18, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 25 on pages 12 and 13: geometric-sum encoding, subtraction of the two length equations, digit enumeration and sufficiency verification.
review.annotationCheck: Correctly handles fixed digits, positive n, the nonzero divisor, exclusion of b = 18 and sufficiency for at least two lengths. No material gap.
